$comment: Named executable profiles. A record's `benchmark_profile` says what shape its candidate set has; this file says what that shape is, so the validator can check it. Registering a profile here is what makes it checkable — a record declaring a profile that is not registered fails validation rather than passing unchecked. Asymmetric profiles must also declare the aggregation procedure required to avoid pool-shape bias. Every profile also declares a `lineage`, and `collection_lineage` below says which lineage each corpus collection belongs to: Featured v1 and the Full Corpus executable subset are built and released as separate manifests, so a record may not carry a profile from the other lineage.

collection_lineage.$comment: Collections whose records are lineage-bound. A record in one of these must declare a profile of the matching lineage. Collections absent here — development, tutorial, stress-tests — are working collections and are unconstrained.

featured-core-2x2x2-v1.description: Two public, two expert and two framework candidates: the Featured v1 pilot standard. Yields 12 unordered cross-source QCCS pairs per complete execution.
featured-core-2x2x2-v1.representation_note: Companion representations of one case family. They must state the same decision question, the same candidate set and the same stipulations, and differ only in scenario detail.

full-corpus-2x2x2-v1.description: Full Corpus profile with the symmetric two-public, two-expert and two-framework shape. The same candidate geometry as the Featured pilot standard, but Full Corpus lineage: a Full Corpus family whose evidence supports two candidates in every pool declares this rather than the Featured profile.
full-corpus-2x2x2-v1.representation_note: Companion representations of one case family. They must state the same decision question, the same candidate set and the same stipulations, and differ only in scenario detail.

full-corpus-1x2x2-mean-v1.description: Evidence-qualified Full Corpus profile with one public, two expert and two framework candidates. Unequal cross-source partner counts require Mean aggregation.
full-corpus-1x2x2-mean-v1.representation_note: Companion representations of one case family. The asymmetric candidate shape is evidence-driven; Mean aggregation is required because Sum would favor the singleton pool on partner count alone.
